info.desc: Hail to the Thief (subtitled The Gloaming, written as Hail to the Thief, (or, The Gloaming.) in the album booklet) is the sixth studio album by English rock band Radiohead, released on 9 June 2003 in the United Kingdom and 10 June 2003, in the United States. It debuted at number one in the UK and at number three in the United States. After two Radiohead albums that featured heavily processed vocals, less guitar, and strong influence from experimental electronica and jazz, Hail to the Thief was seen as a return to alternative rock, drawing its sound from every era .

podcast.body: Radiohead's sixth album, recorded at Oceanway Recording in Hollywood in September 2002. It was their last album under their original contract with EMI Records. The band decided to pull back on experimentation and return to basics, featuring more live-in-the-studio takes rather than computer-generated loops and samples. Recording was fast-paced, about a track a day, and mixing was completed in two weeks. Tom Yorke's lyrics were inspired by the post-9/11 world, including right-wing politics, the War on Terror, and the Bush administration. The album was catastrophically leaked online in an unmixed and unmastered form from March to June, 10 weeks before its official release. "This record, all about performance."

podcast.body: Released as a contractual obligation to EMI Records, this album was put out somewhat "in desperation" and "in a hurry." Radiohead felt emotionally exhausted after the intense recording period for this album, `Kid A`, and `Amnesiac`, and primarily wanted to fulfill their contract to part ways with EMI. "el disco jeit de tip realmente sale por un compromiso que tenía Radiohead con emi."

Released in 2003, this album had lyrical fragments from its songs subtly included in a hidden booklet discovered in certain editions of Radiohead's 2000 album, "Kid A." "There's scraps of lyrics from songs that appeared on two future Radiohead albums, Amnestyak in 2001, and Hale to the Thief in 2003."

podcast.body: This album's touring cycle concluded at the end of 2004, marking a period of transition for the band. The phrase "Burn the Witch" was present on this album, indicating that the band was working on a song with that title as early as 2003. "brought us to the end of the touring cycle for the Hail to the Thief album."
